payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a specialist is dispatched, its brief shall name one task, relevant instructions, requirements, acceptance criteria, source locations and a completion condition.
- When unrelated work is assigned, the orchestrator shall use a fresh bounded context rather than replay the previous task conversation.
- When implementation completes, the orchestrator shall enqueue it for integration before dispatching optional work and shall record integration completion or a concrete wait reason.
- When a run is reviewed, implementation completion and integration start shall be available without transcript reconstruction.
payload.description:
When a release orchestrator repeatedly redirects long-lived specialists and leaves completed fixes waiting, I want bounded task briefs and prompt integration, so I can reduce coordination cost without losing required checks.

## Execution Order

1 of 5 in the high-priority release-efficiency improvements approved for filing on 2026-10-24. Execute stories one by one; filing is not implementation authorization.

## Evidence

Release v0.26.12 main transcript records 43 follow-up dispatches and 36 messages. Fix author timestamps precede integration substantially. See .basicly/usage/release-v02612/release-effort-audit.json. Agent names were reused across unrelated assignments.

## Scope

Orchestrator dispatch instructions, task brief construction, integration queue policy and applicable tests. Reuse existing durable-brief work basicly-ejdm.3; do not duplicate it.
payload.requirements: Preserve existing safety gates and user work. Implement only after a separate story kickoff. Any tracker changes must preserve append-only events and existing conflict-free Git merge behavior; do not introduce a shared mutable snapshot or require updating a PR from main merely because another PR added tracker events.
payload.title: Bound specialist assignments and integrate completed work promptly

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a change is ready, one engine operation shall perform the required regeneration, verification, merge, confirmation, closure and cleanup or report a named blocking condition.
- When interrupted at any transition boundary, resuming shall preserve every event and completed action without repeating a successful merge or losing claim, evidence or closure state.
- When two PR branches append tracker events from the same base and the first is merged, the second shall remain mergeable without updating it from main solely because tracker files changed.
- When that concurrent-branch scenario is exercised in both orders through supported merge, squash and rebase workflows, tracker integration shall preserve all event identities and payloads without textual conflict resolution or history rewriting.
- When concurrent updates concern the same record, the merged tracker shall retain both histories and preserve existing semantic conflict reporting rather than silently discard either update.
- When bookkeeping is consolidated or folded, outstanding PR branches shall retain the preceding merge-safety guarantees.
payload.description:
When a completed change needs repeated agent-driven landing, regeneration, confirmation and closure steps, I want one resumable engine operation, so I can reduce process overhead without losing recovery or tracker merge safety.

## Execution Order

2 of 5. Execute one story at a time.

## Evidence

The release contains separate provisioning, landing and closing tracker commits plus regeneration commits. Current seams are src/basicly/merge.py commit_tracker_state, src/basicly/rebase.py refresh_generated and src/basicly/loop.py _on_ship.

## Owner Constraint

The owner tested concurrent PRs carrying tracker changes. Merging one must not make the other unmergeable due to tracker-file changes or require merging main into it solely to resolve tracker history. Preserve that behavior for PRs and other supported Git integration paths.

## Scope

Existing engine landing/closure path and regression tests. Preserve the published claim. Consolidate bookkeeping only where append-only event preservation, concurrency, gates and recovery remain correct. Do not redesign tracker storage.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When an implementation is handed to integration, the applicable consumer demonstration shall have run against the exact candidate and its result shall be recorded.
- When an installer changes, its demonstration shall exercise the affected operation in a fresh consumer repository.
- When a tutorial changes, its demonstration shall run the documented commands and normal commits with required hooks enabled.
- When only unit-test evidence exists for a required consumer demonstration, the handoff shall refuse and name the missing operation.
- When candidate inputs change, the demonstration result shall be reused only if equivalent trusted inputs are established.
payload.description:
When unit-tested changes reach integration before their actual consumer operation is exercised, I want the existing demonstration contract checked before handoff, so I can find setup and behavioral failures before release stabilization.

## Scope

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a release runs, its report shall distinguish implementation, integration queue wait, verification, failure repair and publication using recorded observations.
- When a check repeats, the report shall name the changed inputs or other reason that invalidated prior evidence, or explicitly state that the reason is unknown.
- When tokens are reported, the report shall distinguish uncached input, cached input and output without presenting token counters as monetary cost.
- When agents run concurrently, elapsed wall time and overlapping agent work shall be reported without summing overlaps into release duration.
- When telemetry is missing, the report shall show unknown rather than zero or an inferred implementation percentage.
- When the report is generated, task attribution and verification reruns shall be understandable without manual transcript analysis.
payload.description:
When release cost must be reconstructed from transcripts and commit timestamps, I want attributed phase timing, task token accounting and check rerun reasons, so I can identify coordination and verification waste while work is running.

- When all three agent baselines are generated, their command examples and quality rules shall prescribe focused checks while editing and required full verification at the appropriate integrated-candidate boundary, with no contradictory whole-suite-first instruction.

- When candidate source or relevant environment inputs change, guidance shall require affected verification rather than assume prior evidence remains valid.
- When scenario checks exercise a small code edit, tracker-only update, failed check and release candidate, the resulting required actions shall be consistent across all three agent targets.
- When this correction ships, all required gates shall remain enabled; fewer runs alone shall not count as proof of equivalent coverage.

When the shared Quality Gate says focused checks first but the Commands section says whole suite then one file, I want one consistent testing sequence across agent instructions, so I can avoid unnecessary full runs without weakening verification.

AGENTS.md:101 and .claude/CLAUDE.md:101 and .github/copilot-instructions.md:101 require focused checks first. payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When the user already explicitly approved an action within the same scope, projected guidance shall direct the agent to reuse that approval and identify it rather than ask again solely because a phase or agent changed.
- When an action exceeds the approved scope or falls under a confirmation category without applicable approval, guidance shall still require confirmation before that action.
- When the user freezes scope, guidance shall permit finishing started work and demonstrated blockers within that scope, and shall require reporting a broader blocker instead of silently starting unrelated improvements.
- When an adjacent finding does not block the approved outcome, guidance shall direct the agent to record it without implementing it.
- When scenarios cover an approved CI edit, a different unapproved CI edit, safe read-only clarification work and a frozen-release adjacent bug, all three targets shall preserve the correct authorization and scope boundary.
payload.description:
When the shared confirmation list says ask before an action but does not state how prior explicit authorization applies, and ownership permits necessary adjacent repairs without a concrete scope-freeze rule, I want one clear decision contract, so I can avoid repeated approval requests and silent scope growth.

## Evidence

.basicly/core/fragments/boundaries/require-explicit-confirmation.fragment.yaml lists restricted actions but does not state that an existing explicit approval for the same action and scope satisfies confirmation. .basicly/core/fragments/design/knowledge-priming.fragment.yaml already gives current user instructions precedence. .basicly-local/fragments/user/project/ownership.fragment.yaml permits necessary adjacent fixes. The release expanded from its original required set before the owner froze scope. This is a missing decision clarification, not evidence that every approval request or added repair was unnecessary.

## Scope

Confirmation, decision-protocol, ownership, session-completion and applicable workflow guidance; projections and decision scenarios. Do not broaden tool permissions or change the existing confirmation categories. Bounded specialist dispatch itself remains basicly-42pn387.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When the projected always-on baseline mixes prose and constraints with no fixed structure, I want the constraint content projected as an explicit three-tier block, so I can make the rules easier to retrieve and follow.

## Context

Plan §4 Phase 4 steps 4 and 5, merged - step 5 alone is a fragment reorder and does not earn its own package.

Project the constraint content as an explicit three-tier block - always do, ask first, never do. A retrieval problem wants a structural fix, not more prose.

Move the Commands section early, and prefer one real example over three paragraphs where a convention has a canonical form.

## Release Efficiency Audit 2026-10-24

Promote and reuse this existing story rather than file a duplicate. Preserve its three-tier constraint structure, early Commands section and real examples. Also remove unconditional specialist procedure from the always-on path by routing it to existing on-demand skills where safe. The universal derive-every-number-twice rule in external-facts is a concrete candidate for a risk-based condition. Do not remove safety constraints, factual verification or positive controls needed to establish an absence claim.

Measured with wc -lc: AGENTS.md has 222 lines and 14152 bytes; .claude/CLAUDE.md has 174 lines and 11273 bytes; .github/copilot-instructions.md has 175 lines and 11365 bytes at v0.26.12. Size alone does not establish poor adherence. Read the corresponding target filters before routing any fragment, because scoped text reaches targets differently.

## Scope

Shared and applicable overlay fragment sources, target-aware projection only where required, existing on-demand skills and focused behavioral evaluation. Do not introduce another instruction source or copy safety text into multiple editable files. Coordinate with the new shared testing and decision-contract stories. Bounded specialist assignment behavior remains basicly-42pn387.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
Given the projected baseline when it is rendered then the constraint content appears as an explicit three-tier block of always do and ask first and never do and the Commands section appears early and each convention with a canonical form carries one real example instead of prose
- When guidance is restructured, every existing instruction shall be accounted for as retained, deduplicated, routed with an explicit trigger, or deliberately corrected with a reason.
- When a specialist procedure moves on demand, the remaining baseline shall give a reliable trigger and all applicable agent targets shall retain access to that procedure without assuming identical host scoping behavior.
- When routine work only needs reporting an observed count, guidance shall not demand independent numerical derivation without a material correctness reason; high-risk quantitative claims and absence claims shall retain appropriate independent controls.
- When projected outputs are measured before and after, the result shall report bytes, lines and the measurement method for each target; a smaller file or higher recall score alone shall not prove successful behavior.
- When behavioral scenarios cover ordinary code work, approved actions, frozen scope, focused verification and source-to-projection editing, the streamlined guidance shall preserve required safety and workflow outcomes across all three targets.
- When catalog sources are projected, existing catalog, projection and instruction-size checks shall pass without raising caps or weakening gates.
